findings.claim: The '+N¢ (+X.X%) Today' price-change pill on the discovery hero is fabricated from a hash of the market ticker, not from any price data. deterministicDelta (app/components/prediction/utils/spark.ts:28-37) computes delta = (seed % 11) - 4 from the ticker string; DiscoveryHero.tsx:75 renders it at lines 148-176 next to the label 'TODAY', and it also drives the chart's green/red color. It runs on ALL deploys (not gated by NEXT_PUBLIC_DEMO_SYNTHETIC_CHARTS) and carries no on-screen demo/synthetic label. The same fake number appears on every FeaturedCarousel slide.
findings.designImplication: Remove or replace with a real 24h delta computed from GET /markets/:id/prices (useHeroPriceHistory already fetches the series — derive delta = last - first from it). While no real series exists, render a neutral dash, never a signed percentage. A fabricated 'Today' change on a trading product is the single most damaging honesty defect found.

findings.claim: The 'Top Movers' rail is entirely synthetic: every row's 24h % delta comes from deterministicDelta (ticker hash) and every sparkline from sparklinePath, a seeded random walk whose up/down bias is set by the fake delta (TrendingSidebar.tsx:109,133; spark.ts:151-169). The header shows a pulsing live dot labeled '24H'. The component's own comment admits 'Sparklines and 24h delta are deterministic from the ticker (placeholder until backend exposes price history)' — but nothing on screen says so. Markets are ranked as 'movers' while their displayed movement is invented.
findings.designImplication: Either wire rows to the real price-history endpoint (batch endpoint or accept N small fetches for 6 rows) or strip the fabricated delta pill + sparkline and rank by real volume with an honest 'by volume' label. Remove the pulsing '24H' live dot until the data is real.

findings.claim: The hero chart silently falls back to a deterministic synthetic walk on every deploy — not just demo. heroChartPath (spark.ts:106-148) draws a 24-point seeded walk whenever useHeroPriceHistory returns null, which it does while loading, on fetch failure, AND when the market has no price movement (useHeroPriceHistory.ts:38-40). This fallback is NOT gated by NEXT_PUBLIC_DEMO_SYNTHETIC_CHARTS. The fabricated curve renders full-bleed under a pulsing 'LIVE' badge (DiscoveryHero.tsx:113-121, 272-328) with no visible label, so a quiet or failing market permanently shows an invented price history on the home page.
findings.designImplication: Gate the hero fallback behind the same DEMO_SYNTHETIC_CHARTS flag MarketChart uses (spark.ts should accept a syntheticFallbackEnabled arg). Honest states: skeleton while loading, flat line at current price for no-movement, hide the plot on error. At minimum overlay a visible 'Illustrative' caption whenever the walk is drawn.

findings.claim: The market-detail chart (MarketChart.tsx + market-chart-state.ts) is honest by default — loading skeleton, error+retry panel, flat line for no-movement — but when NEXT_PUBLIC_DEMO_SYNTHETIC_CHARTS=true the synthetic walk returns state 'ready' (market-chart-state.ts:84-94) and is pixel-identical to a real chart: no badge, watermark, or caption distinguishes it. The public demo is built with this flag ON (.github/workflows/deploy-demo.yml:351 passes --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_DEMO_SYNTHETIC_CHARTS=true), so investors/users on the live demo see fabricated price movement with zero disclosure. Each range tab (1H/6H/1D/1W/ALL) even reseeds a different fake walk, simulating range-specific history that doesn't exist; 6H additionally silently serves 1D data (MarketChart.tsx:40-49).
findings.designImplication: When the flag is on, render a persistent visible 'Demo data — simulated chart' badge in the chart corner (resolveChartSeries can return a `synthetic: true` bit for the component to render). Longer term, drop the flag from deploy-demo.yml once seeded price history (demo-data Phase 2 trades) feeds the real endpoint.

findings.claim: MarketCard's sentiment line converts price into a claim about people: en/prediction.json:43-47 renders 'Heavy Backing • {{percentage}}% say Yes' / 'Strong Doubt • {{percentage}}% say No' from calculateMarketSentiment(yesPricePoints) (marketSentiment.ts:20-53, MarketCard.tsx:100,177-189). A 75¢ price becomes '75% say Yes' — implying a count of respondents that doesn't exist. Price is a probability estimate, not a population share; the landing page's own copy ('Market says 61% Yes') is the honest formulation.
findings.designImplication: Reword the five MARKET_SENTIMENT_* strings (all 7 locales) to price framing: 'Market prices Yes at 75%' or 'Yes leads at 75¢'. No code change needed beyond locale files.

findings.claim: DiscoveryHero labels lifetime cumulative volume as '24h volume'. The stat at DiscoveryHero.tsx:242-250 renders market.volumePoints under t('24H_VOLUME') ('24h volume', en/prediction.json:38), but volume_points is a monotonically incremented per-trade counter on the market row (gateway amm.go:185, exchange.go:516,633) with no time-window query anywhere. A market with all its volume from weeks ago displays that total as yesterday's activity — systematically inflating apparent liquidity/recency.
findings.designImplication: Relabel to 'Total volume' (matches MarketCard's plain 'Volume', which is correct), or add a real 24h-windowed volume field to the API and keep the label. Cheapest honest fix is the label.

findings.claim: The logged-out landing page presents four invented markets as live product data: EXAMPLE_MARKETS (app/page.tsx:12-37) hardcodes yesPercent 61/62/57/54 with copy 'Market says 61% Yes' etc. (page-home.json:12-21), rendered under the section eyebrow 'Live markets' and heading 'Markets Filipinos are watching' with working YES/NO toggle buttons that recompute the bar (page.tsx:191-271, 641-680). Nothing on screen marks them as examples. The hero adds 'Live prediction markets · Philippines' plus pulsing 'live' quote chips 'YES 62¢ / NO 38¢' on a hand-drawn decorative chart (page.tsx:579-601 — the code comment calls them 'live YES/NO quotes').
findings.designImplication: Best fix: fetch 4 real markets from the public /api/v1/discovery endpoint (it requires no auth) so the landing page shows true prices. Otherwise add a visible 'Example markets — illustrative' caption to the card stack, change the 'Live markets' eyebrow to 'How markets look', and drop the pulsing dots from the decorative hero quotes.

findings.claim: TradeTicketPreview on the landing page (app/page.tsx:295-417) is a hardcoded miniature ticket — 62¢/38¢ prices, 500 pts stake, '800 pts if correct', pulsing 'Live' dot. It is disclosed as a mockup only to screen readers (role='img', aria-label 'TapTrade player app mobile mockup'); sighted users see no such label. Lower severity because it visually reads as a device mockup, but the 'Live' badge on invented numbers undercuts that.
findings.designImplication: Add a small visible caption under the mockup ('Illustrative preview') and remove the animated 'Live' pulse from static example numbers.

findings.claim: Community and trading surfaces are genuinely wired: MarketDiscussion.tsx fetches/creates comments via market-social-client (no seeded comments in the frontend), RecentTrades.tsx renders real Trade[] from the API/WebSocket, OrderBook and the market-detail liquidity card use real API fields (liquidityPoints, ammLiquidityParam), and MarketHead/CountdownTimer countdowns derive from real closeAt timestamps. No fake testimonials, user counts, licensing badges, or urgency mechanics exist anywhere in app/ — the footer's 'Non-redeemable point prediction markets' line (PredictFooter.tsx:54) and the About/Terms/Register pages disclose the play-points model plainly.
findings.designImplication: Keep these patterns as the honesty baseline for the redesign. One caveat: on the demo deploy the trades tape and leaderboards display backend-seeded demo activity (make demo-data Phase 2/5, trade_kind='demo_history') indistinguishably from organic activity — a demo-environment banner would cover this without touching components.

findings.claim: Balance displays disagree on units, risking a 100x-misstated balance: WalletBreakdown.tsx:93-95 divides by 100 ('formatPointsFromPoints(cents)') while CurrentBalance.tsx:100-102 and TopBar render the same class of point values with no division — yet market-display.ts:8-9 declares the 2026-07-07 unit model as '1 Point = 1 cent of play value; API integers ARE whole Points. No /100 conversion.' One of these components shows a wrong number.
findings.designImplication: Audit the bonus-client WalletBreakdown payload units against the wallet-client Balance units and standardize on the points-native model with one shared formatter; a user seeing 50.00 pts in one widget and 5,000 pts in another destroys trust faster than any styling issue.

findings.claim: CountdownTimer.tsx (app/components/CountdownTimer.tsx, 145 lines) is imported nowhere in app/ or pages/ — it is dead code, and its styling (slate-on-dark) predates the P8/P9 light design system. No countdown-urgency dark patterns are currently live; all shipped countdowns (MarketHead 'closes in', DiscoveryHero 'Closes') state real market close times.
findings.designImplication: Delete the unused component during the redesign so it can't be casually reattached as a sales-pressure widget later.

findings.claim: The demo flag's blast radius is asymmetric by design intent but not by implementation: features.ts:96-103 documents DEMO_SYNTHETIC_CHARTS as 'demo boxes ONLY... real deploys show honest loading/error/empty chart states', yet the two discovery-surface fabrications (hero walk fallback, Top Movers sparklines/deltas) ignore the flag entirely, so the documented guarantee only holds for the market-detail chart.
findings.designImplication: Make the flag the single chokepoint for ALL synthetic rendering: route spark.ts fallbacks through it, and have every synthetic path emit a visible on-screen 'Demo' marker so a mis-set env var can never silently fabricate data in production.

summary:
The player app has a split honesty profile. The market-detail chart pipeline (MarketChart.tsx + market-chart-state.ts) was deliberately reworked to be honest-by-default — real /prices data, skeleton/error/flat-line states, synthetic walks only behind NEXT_PUBLIC_DEMO_SYNTHETIC_CHARTS — and the social/trading surfaces (discussion, trade tape, order book, liquidity card, balances) are genuinely API-wired with no invented users, testimonials, compliance badges, or countdown-urgency mechanics. The play-money model is disclosed visibly ("Non-redeemable point prediction markets" in the footer; About/Terms/Register repeat it).

But the discovery surfaces still fabricate market movement on every deploy, with no flag gate and no on-screen labeling. deterministicDelta hashes the ticker string into a fake "+N¢ (+X%) Today" change that renders in the hero (next to a pulsing LIVE badge) and in every "Top Movers" row (under a pulsing "24H" dot); Top Movers sparklines are seeded random walks whose direction is set by that same fake delta; and the hero chart silently substitutes a synthetic walk whenever real history is loading, failed, or flat. Compounding this, the hero labels lifetime cumulative volume as "24h volume", MarketCard converts price into "'X% say Yes" population claims, and the logged-out landing page presents four hardcoded example markets under a "Live markets" eyebrow with interactive YES/NO buttons and pulsing "live" quote chips. Meanwhile the flag-gated market-detail synthetic mode IS enabled on the public demo build (deploy-demo.yml passes NEXT_PUBLIC_DEMO_SYNTHETIC_CHARTS=true) and renders pixel-identically to real data — no badge distinguishes it.

Priority fixes: (1) kill or gate the ungated fabrications in spark.ts — derive the hero delta from the already-fetched real series, replace Top Movers deltas/sparklines with real data or volume-ranked honest rows; (2) add a visible "Demo data — simulated" badge whenever any synthetic path renders, including the demo deploy's market chart; (3) relabel "24h volume" → "Total volume" and reword the MARKET_SENTIMENT_* strings to price framing; (4) swap the landing page's hardcoded markets for the public discovery API or caption them as illustrative; (5) reconcile the /100 unit divergence between WalletBreakdown and CurrentBalance/TopBar; (6) delete the unused CountdownTimer component. These are mostly label-and-wiring changes — the honest data paths already exist and the redesign should route everything through them.
